subject: Segregated Edge Topology — Acceptance checklist & carrier NAT constraints
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: EdgeOps <edgeops@aurora-payments.com>, CarrierNet NOC <noc@carriernet.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Segregated Edge Topology — Acceptance checklist & carrier NAT constraints

Hi all,

Attached is the annotated edge topology (v2) and the acceptance checklist we ran through in staging. Key asks for this thread:
- Confirm CarrierNet MTU behaviour on the 3rd hop (we observed 1400 bytes in the staging run).
- Confirm whether CarrierNet will preserve TCP MSS clamping or whether we need to implement path MTU workarounds in the sidecar.
- Sign off on the control-plane ingress filtration (IP allowlist + TLS mTLS toe-in) and the proposed fallback to a regional dedicated proxy if the edge cluster reports >5% degraded KV-cache miss rates.

Quick status: staging validation passed functional tests but uncovered two operational items: MTU blackhole with large inference payloads and intermittent SYN retransmits during peak bursts. I included an export of packet-level counters in egress-evidence.csv.

Attachments: seg-edge-annotated-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram), egress-evidence.csv (pcap counters summary), carrier-mtu-report.txt (CarrierNet report we requested)

Requesting: CarrierNet NOC to confirm MTU behaviours and EdgeOps to schedule a joint MTU/healthcheck test window.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: EdgeOps <edgeops@aurora-payments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: CarrierNet NOC <noc@carriernet.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segregated Edge Topology — Acceptance checklist & carrier NAT constraints

Olga,

Thanks for the diagram and the CSV. We reproduced the MTU drop locally when the third hop to CarrierNet performed hairpin NAT for VPC-translated egress (their handed-over link looks to be at 1402 bytes). CarrierNet confirmed they do not perform MSS clamping for encapsulated flows. Their report (attached) explains this is by design on the shared transit fabric to avoid edge fragmentation at scale.

Practical implications for Redwood/Aurora:
- Large model responses (>= 12k token responses when chunked) hit an MTU path reduction and may require segmentation at the application layer.
- Sidecar-level MSS clamping or per-connection PMTUD probes are options; the simpler short-term fix is application segmentation at 1200 bytes payload to be safe across heterogenous carriers.

EdgeOps proposed a test window next Monday (22 Nov) 10:00–12:00 PST to run a joint synthetic load with 1) 12k token responses, 2) streaming chunked responses, and 3) control-plane reconnect storm simulation. We can provide packet captures and sidecar logs.

—Chris, EdgeOps
Head of Edge Reliability
Aurora Payments

-----Forwarded Message-----
From: CarrierNet NOC <noc@carriernet.io>
To: EdgeOps <edgeops@aurora-payments.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 12:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CarrierNet MTU behaviour

CarrierNet confirms: shared-transit links use an encapsulation that reduces effective MTU to 1402 bytes for encapsulated customer flows. We explicitly do not modify MSS for TCP to avoid edge-side performance regressions for some legacy flows. If customers need higher effective MTU we offer a dedicated channel (L3-sliced) but that requires a separate contract and 4–6 week provisioning window.

—CarrierNet NOC

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, EdgeOps <edgeops@aurora-payments.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Segregated Edge Topology — Acceptance checklist & carrier NAT constraints

Thanks Chris and CarrierNet team — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions and operational proposals:

1) Can we get an explicit list of flows that CarrierNet treats as "encapsulated" vs "native" (e.g., GRE/VXLAN vs pure public IPv4)? We want to ensure our control-plane keepalives (gRPC over mTLS) are not being down-sized in a way that induces reconnects.

2) For the short-term: propose we implement sidecar MSS clamping with a toggle in the Canary config (toggle flag: sidecar.egress.mss=1200). That would let us ship the fix to staging and toggle off during the dedicated-channel pilot.

3) For the longer term: if Aurora wants to avoid application segmentation we should discuss procuring a dedicated L3-slice from CarrierNet. Jonas / Marissa — please capture estimated provisioning lead time and a rough delta in monthly cost if we pursue that.

Action items I recommend we commit to for Monday's joint test:
- EdgeOps: provide packet captures for 3 test cases and a sample streaming workload.
- CarrierNet: confirm which nodes perform encapsulation and whether a per-flow tag can avoid encapsulation.
- Redwood: enable sidecar MSS toggle in Canary and prepare a short experiment runbook.

Kimberly Park
Product Lead — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, 20 Nov 2026 at 13:10, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — I captured the provisioning ask in the INF ticket (INF-2043). For the dedicated channel estimate: CarrierNet quoted ~5 weeks provisioning + a one-time L3 circuit fee. Marissa, can you surface the procurement contact and start a scoping convo?
>
> Quick operational note: if we implement sidecar MSS clamping we should also record a metric (egress.mss_applied) and wire it to the Console telemetry so we can alert on high rates of clamping (signal of upstream MTU mismatch).
>
> I'll join Monday's test.
>
> —Jonas
> Senior Network Architect
> Redwood Inference

On Sat, 21 Nov 2026 at 15:47, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks everyone — summary and next steps:
>
> 1) Monday 22 Nov 10:00–12:00 PST — joint test window confirmed (EdgeOps + CarrierNet + Redwood infra). Meeting invite sent separately.
>
> 2) Redwood: prepare Canary with sidecar.egress.mss=1200 and a short experiment (backstop: application-level chunking to 1.1k payloads). Neha, please add the experiment runbook to the INF ticket and include the Console metrics (egress.mss_applied, controlplane.reconnect_rate).
>
> 3) EdgeOps: provide packet captures and synthetic workload payloads ahead of the window (attach to INF-2043).
>
> 4) CarrierNet: confirm encapsulating nodes list and whether we can request per-flow bypass for our control-plane keepalives.
>
> 5) Procurement: Marissa to spin up a vendor scoping for a dedicated L3 slice if Aurora chooses that option; include estimated cost and provisioning lead time.
>
> I'll mark acceptance pending on successful MTU tests and <1% control-plane reconnects during a 2-hour burst test.
>
> Cheers,
> Olga
> Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
